evidence.observation: The sole production delta restores the std_text::read byte ceiling from 1048575 to 1048576. Read failure still maps to whole-request invalid-request, and the complete returned byte owner is passed to the unchanged std_json parser.
Parsing completes before request envelope processing and result emission; the change introduces no truncation, alternate validation path or partial result emission.
New tests call the actual byte host subprocess with raw stdin and assert zero process exit and decoded output, retaining the portable host resolver.
Independent literal 1048576 limit; below/at/above cases include empty envelope, valid empty plan and multibyte Unicode schema-invalid content, with mixed trailing JSON whitespace counted as bytes.

Explicit boundary-final garbage and invalid UTF-8, incomplete JSON, and an oversized valid prefix followed by garbage challenge both strict parsing and prefix truncation. Existing strict transport and graph assertions remain in the supplied patch.

score_rationale.clarity: Clear named standard-library read followed by parse; one localized budget correction.
score_rationale.consistency: All inputs retain the same read/parse/envelope path and explicit failure handling.
score_rationale.testing: Meaningful independent exact-byte boundary expectations plus real-stdin malformed-boundary and truncation checks supplement retained regression assertions.

python.correctness_conclusion: No independent root-cause defect identified in the sealed change.

evidence.observation: The localized >= to > fix checks raw byte length before UTF-8 decoding. Existing depth, duplicate-key, signed integer, finite float, strict JSON and Unicode scalar validation remains after the size check.
The response adapter retains whole-request errors; stdin reads the shared MAX_INPUT_BYTES constant plus one, so an oversized request cannot be mistaken for a valid allowed-length prefix.
Tests pin an independent contract limit and route each case through both respond and an actual stdin subprocess, asserting exit zero and newline-terminated JSON output.

Below/at/above tests include a valid plan and substantial multibyte text with decoded character length below the byte ceiling; additional oversized whitespace and second-document suffixes challenge truncation.
Boundary-sized malformed documents cover duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8, unpaired surrogates, integer overflow, nonfinite values and excessive nesting, including a bad final byte.

score_rationale.clarity: A named input constant and one explicit inclusive-boundary comparison express the contract directly.
score_rationale.consistency: Direct calls and stdin share parse_request/respond and the same size constant; the one-extra-byte reader retains oversized detection.
score_rationale.testing: Independent numeric limits, multiple valid and malformed boundaries, byte-versus-character discrimination and actual stdin coverage supplement original tests.

zig.correctness_conclusion: No independent root-cause defect identified in the sealed change.

evidence.observation: The stdin reader retains the shared max_input plus one bound; StreamTooLong yields whole-request invalid-request and a successful return. Otherwise the complete acquired slice goes to respond.
The localized >= to > fix preserves the byte-based inclusive bound. UTF-8, depth, duplicate-key JSON parsing, numeric validation and envelope checks remain unchanged afterward.
The direct-response test now checks below, at and above the limit, preserving explicit expected response strings.
Additional direct tests exercise Unicode byte boundaries and malformed or final-garbage documents at the exact ceiling.

A separate literal contract limit drives actual compiled stdin execution, with exit-zero/newline checks, empty envelopes, a nonempty successful plan, oversize requests and substantial multibyte strings.
Independent boundary expectations retain strict parsing, surrogate, UTF-8, integer, nonfinite and nesting rejection and explicitly reject an oversized valid prefix.

score_rationale.clarity: Named max_input and one explicit comparison make the corrected boundary clear.
score_rationale.consistency: Both stdin acquisition and respond use the same max_input; overlong acquisition and overlong slices converge on whole-request invalid-request.
score_rationale.testing: New direct and actual-stdin tests combine independent limits, byte/character distinction, successful plans, malformed exact-boundary input and oversize-prefix regression coverage.

my.correctness_conclusion: No independent root-cause defect identified in the sealed priority change.

evidence.observation: Priority presence changes the exact field count from three to four; a numeric integer tag and inclusive -1000..1000 bounds reject booleans, floats, null and out-of-range values. Original required fields remain validated.
IDs remain ASCII-sorted; each parsed priority is stored at the ID lookup index, avoiding a source-order/ID-order mismatch.
A fresh zero-filled priority buffer supplies omitted defaults independently for each manifest and is passed with the other owned scratch buffers.

Cycle feasibility is checked before order output. Every order iteration scans all currently ready vertices and replaces a candidate only for strictly greater priority, retaining the earliest ASCII ID on ties; completion then updates readiness.
Finish times still depend only on prerequisites and duration. Layers rebuild graph readiness and snapshot each round independently of priority; timing output retains ID traversal.
Literal expectations exercise negative/default/equal/extreme priorities and ASCII report arrays, newly ready high priority across job/dependency permutations, and prerequisites overriding priority.

Tests cover wrong types, required and extra fields, duplicate/escaped priority keys, transport overflow, negative zero, validation phase ordering, cyclic blocked output and explicit-zero legacy equivalence.

score_rationale.clarity: Clear comments state the ready-scan and tie-break invariant; priority handling is localized to schema, storage and candidate selection.
score_rationale.consistency: ID ordering remains the common report invariant; priority affects only ready candidate selection and defaults are initialized uniformly.
score_rationale.testing: Independent expected order/error arrays and boundary values supplement retained regression coverage; permutation, dependency, cycle and legacy-zero cases are meaningful.

quality_observations: The change adds one parallel owned priority buffer and another work parameter; ID-index association is explicit through lookup rather than relying on input order.

The newly-ready test derives unchanged non-order reports from the legacy path, so those particular expectations are metamorphic rather than independent; literal ordering, boundary and error assertions provide independent coverage.
Ready selection is a bounded scan, not a new application-specific heap implementation. No performance conclusion is drawn.

python.correctness_conclusion: No independent root-cause defect identified in the sealed priority change.

evidence.observation: Required-key subset and allowed-key superset checks preserve the original fields while allowing only priority; exact int type and inclusive bounds reject bool and float values.
Priority is carried in a frozen Job with default zero; complete schema and duplicate/missing dependency phases still precede scheduling.
Both initial and newly-ready heap entries use (-priority, ID), ensuring highest priority first and ASCII ties. Dependents enter the heap only when their remaining prerequisite count reaches zero.
Timings remain prerequisite-based; round depth is derived from dependencies and layers/timings are constructed by sorted IDs. Cyclic blocked IDs remain sorted independently of heap order.
Tests use literal expected priority order, layers, timing values and makespan; all job permutations and dependency spellings are checked, with mixed explicit/default zero legacy compatibility.
Schema/transport boundary tests distinguish per-manifest failure from whole-request failure; precedence and cyclic/downstream/self-cycle reports are challenged across permutations.

score_rationale.clarity: The named Job.priority field and comment explaining negation make the heap ordering rule explicit.
score_rationale.consistency: The same tuple key is used for initial readiness and subsequent releases; unrelated report arrays retain sorted-ID construction.
score_rationale.testing: Literal full-report expectations, bounds, permutations, legacy defaults and cycle/validation regressions provide independent behavioral coverage.

quality_observations: Initial heap construction and incremental insertion repeat the same small tuple expression; they are visibly consistent in this delta.
New priority tests primarily exercise plan/respond directly rather than adding a new stdin test; actual stdin was not specifically required by this priority brief. No runtime success is inferred.

zig.correctness_conclusion: No independent root-cause defect identified in the sealed priority change.

evidence.observation: The extracted parseJob helper distinguishes absent optional priority from present JSON null, validates inclusive integer bounds, checks exact field count and explicitly retrieves every required field before returning Job.
Jobs remain ID-sorted before duplicate/dependency validation, preserving priority-independent report ordering.

The scheduler rescans ready jobs after each removal and replaces the selected candidate only for greater priority; the ID-sorted traversal breaks ties. No candidate yields the existing sorted blocked report.
Start/finish/makespan use prerequisites and durations. The removed set resets for dependency-round layers, and timing reports traverse the ID-sorted jobs.

A literal full expected report covers negative, default and explicit-zero ties, both priority endpoints and a newly-ready high-priority job. Tests reverse dependency spelling and try pairwise input-job swaps.

Additional tests distinguish schema types/bounds/required fields from whole-request duplicate keys and numeric overflow, and retain ASCII order for duplicate, missing-reference and cycle/downstream reports.

score_rationale.clarity: Named parseJob centralizes schema construction, and comments clearly describe the ID-sorted tie-break invariant.
score_rationale.consistency: Priority is stored on Job and applied only at ready selection; the shared ID-sorted collection still drives reports and layered traversal.
score_rationale.testing: Literal complete reports and boundary/error assertions plus dependency/job reorderings and retained legacy tests meet independent boundary and regression coverage.

quality_observations: The schema refactor removes the old inline parsing block rather than retaining two competing validators.
The new ordering permutation test exercises every pairwise job swap, not every possible permutation; this is useful but should not be reported as exhaustive permutation coverage.
No new actual-stdin priority test is present in the supplied delta; direct respond tests satisfy the stated source-review rubric, and no execution result is claimed.

review.scope: Sealed SCC membership, self-loop inclusion, downstream exclusion, ordering, validation precedence and bounded-state review against the public cycle-groups brief and v1 contract.
limits: Static source review only: tests were inspected but not run, and no runtime acceptance result is claimed.
No identified defect is not proof of correctness for every supported request.

External compiler, standard-library and host implementations were outside the review bundle and not inspected. Runtime instruction/frame limits and wall-time feasibility are not established by this review.
Supported bounds are 128 jobs per manifest and 64 cases subject also to the total 1 MiB input budget; not every product of maximum dimensions fits that byte budget.
No authored new test explicitly exercises a full 64-case batch of maximum-size cyclic graphs. This is a coverage limitation, not an observed failure.
Scores describe source observations, not syntax/LOC rankings or development/runtime comparisons.

my.correctness_conclusion: No independent root-cause defect identified in the sealed cycle-group change.

evidence.observation: Kosaraju first-pass DFS marks before recursion and appends vertices on return; the second pass follows transposed edges only into unassigned vertices. This computes complete SCCs rather than isolated back-edge paths.
Seen and group arrays reset for the current graph; all vertices participate in the first pass and reverse finishing order drives the second pass. Each component gets a distinct root label.

Blocked output still comes from the completed scheduling state. Components are emitted only at the first ID-sorted member, with every member ID-scanned in order. Size-one components require a self-loop, excluding downstream-only singleton components.

Unknown references return before graph construction. SCC reporting occurs only on the existing cycle error branch after removable work is exhausted, and the caller returns immediately after reusing scheduling scratch.
The reused durations, finish and needs buffers each hold 128 elements; graph edges retain their own storage and are not overwritten by the SCC passes.
An independently structured transitive-closure oracle accompanies literal independent-cycle, one-way bridge, merged component, self-loop, ASCII and precedence examples.
Random small graphs are compared with reachability in batches of 48; separate authored tests cover a 128-job dense SCC and a 128-job ring reaching maximal DFS depth.

score_rationale.clarity: Named visit/assign/self_loop helpers and comments explain traversal orientation, scratch reuse and canonical output ordering.
score_rationale.consistency: Original scheduling state remains the blocked source while SCC labels independently define cycles; both consume the same ID-indexed graph and emit consistent ASCII order.
score_rationale.testing: Independent expected SCCs, a distinct closure oracle, randomized permutations, and explicit dense/deep 128-job tests provide semantic and size-boundary coverage alongside retained regressions.

quality_observations: Scratch reuse is confined to an immediate-return error branch, so overwritten duration/dependency buffers cannot affect a successful plan.

Although it uses Kosaraju, adjacency is found by scanning the entire edge slice at every DFS vertex; the traversal costs O(V*E), not adjacency-list O(V+E). At 128 vertices and 16384 edges, each pass can examine about 2.1 million edges.
The DFS recursion depth is bounded by 128 vertices at source level; compatibility with external VM frame/instruction budgets was not independently checked.
New SCC tests are actual subprocess-driver tests, but their execution outcomes were not accessed.

supported_bounds_review.vertex_storage: Three reused 128-element arrays; each vertex is appended to finishing order once and assigned once. No new smaller vertex cap is introduced.
supported_bounds_review.case_state: Buffers are allocated per manifest and SCC state is reinitialized; no new global mutable state or case coupling appears.
supported_bounds_review.authored_limit_tests: Dense 128-job SCC, 128-job ring and 48-case randomized batches; no new 64-case maximal cyclic batch.

python.correctness_conclusion: No independent root-cause defect identified in the sealed cycle-group change.

evidence.observation: Complete schema, duplicate-ID, repeated-dependency and missing-reference phases still precede plan_graph and SCC traversal.

Tarjan uses discovery indices, lowlinks and an active stack. Child lowlinks and active-neighbor discovery indices are handled separately; a root pops the full SCC. Singleton roots are included only for an actual self-dependency.
Each emitted component and the outer groups list are explicitly sorted. Traversing job-to-prerequisite edges is the transpose of readiness propagation but preserves strong connectivity.
The existing remaining-count blocked set is unchanged. cyclic_groups is invoked only on the cycle-error return, leaving successful reports and non-cycle errors unchanged.

Literal examples cover independent cycles, one-way connections, reverse connections that merge groups, overlapping cycles, self-loops, removable ancestors, downstream tails, ASCII sorting and a 128-job ring.
Every directed graph on three vertices, including self edges, is compared against an independent positive-length transitive-closure computation; acyclic cases must not receive a cycles field.

score_rationale.clarity: The named cyclic_groups helper isolates Tarjan state and documents why prerequisite traversal is valid.
score_rationale.consistency: Blocked membership remains tied to scheduling residuals while cyclic membership uses SCCs; explicit sorting preserves the distinct report contracts.
score_rationale.testing: Independent literal examples and exhaustive three-vertex closure comparisons challenge whole-component correctness, with a 128-job recursion-depth case and retained validation/success regressions.

quality_observations: The traversal visits each vertex/edge once before canonical sorting, using local per-call state; active-stack membership prevents cross-component visited edges from merging completed SCCs.
The maximum ring test covers recursive depth, but there is no new maximum-density SCC test or 64-case cyclic batch test.
New tests call plan/respond directly; no new actual-stdin SCC test was required by the public brief, and no execution is claimed.

supported_bounds_review.vertex_storage: Dictionary/list/set state is bounded by the existing 128-job schema; recursive DFS depth is at most 128 job visits.
supported_bounds_review.case_state: cyclic_groups allocates fresh local state on each call, and respond retains per-manifest processing.
supported_bounds_review.authored_limit_tests: 128-job ring and all 512 three-vertex directed graphs; a mixed cycle/empty request is also authored, but no new 64-case cyclic batch.

zig.correctness_conclusion: No independent root-cause defect identified in the sealed cycle-group change.

evidence.observation: Schema validation and duplicate/dependency phases remain unchanged and precede schedule; jobs are ASCII-sorted once before graph construction.

cycleGroups copies the prerequisite matrix and computes positive-length transitive closure without adding an identity diagonal. Therefore a diagonal becomes true exactly for cyclic membership, including actual self-loops.

Mutual reachability collects each complete SCC; assigned prevents repeated groups. ID-sorted traversal emits members and groups in canonical order, and noncyclic downstream vertices fail the diagonal test.
The cycles field is added only to the existing cycle failure, retaining blocked residual membership and excluding any partial successful order from the returned result.
The existing downstream/upstream cycle regression is updated with the expected singleton cycle group.

Three new independent literal fixtures cover disjoint and one-way-connected SCCs, complete merged groups including bridge vertices, self-loop versus noncyclic singleton membership, ASCII ordering and downstream exclusion.

score_rationale.clarity: A named cycleGroups helper and comments explain positive-length reachability and why first-member emission yields lexicographic order.
score_rationale.consistency: Cycle groups derive from the original graph while blocked derives from the removal state; the shared ID-sorted jobs give consistent canonical arrays.
score_rationale.testing: Independent expected arrays exercise the semantic boundaries between singleton/self-loop, one-way-connected/merged SCCs and blocked/cyclic membership, alongside retained regressions. This score does not imply maximum-size or exhaustive coverage.

quality_observations: The fixed 128-by-128 boolean matrix matches the schema bound; cubic closure performs at most 128^3 inner updates per invocation, with an early skip for unreachable pivots.
The new SCC tests are small hand-authored graphs. Unlike the other sealed submissions, this delta adds no 128-job cyclic case or independently generated closure cross-check.
Existing 128-job and 64-case tests exercise an acyclic chain and envelope behavior, respectively; they do not validate the new SCC path at those limits.
No timing feasibility or memory-allocation-failure behavior of the added SCC output construction was exercised in this static review.

supported_bounds_review.vertex_storage: Matrix and assigned array use max_jobs=128, and closure loops stop at validated graph.count. The matrix is local to cycleGroups.
supported_bounds_review.case_state: SCC working state is local to each invocation; caller-arena results follow the existing per-request allocation pattern. No new case cap appears.
supported_bounds_review.authored_limit_tests: Retained 128-job acyclic and 64-case envelope tests; no newly authored full-size SCC or 64-case cyclic batch.
